q-38184.name: Question 1
q-38184.problem: If $(x+3)$ is a factor of $p(x)=2{x}^{3}+5{x}^{2}+kx-3,$ then $k=$
q-38184.worked_solution:
According to the factor theorem, if $(x-r)$ is a factor of $p(x),$ then the root $x=r$ is also a root of $p(x).$ 

Here, we are considering the factor $(x+3).$ The root of this factor can be found by setting the factor equal to $0$ and solving:

$$
\begin{aligned}x+3 & =0 \\ x & =-3\end{aligned}
$$

According to the factor theorem, then, since $(x+3)$ is a factor of $p(x),$ the root $x=-3$ is also a root of $p(x).$ This means $p(-3)=0,$ so we have

$$
\begin{aligned}2(-3)^{3}+5(-3)^{2}+k(-3)-3 & =0 \\ -54+45-3k-3 & =0 \\ -3k & =12 \\ k & =-4.\end{aligned}
$$

q-7664.name: Question 2
q-7664.problem: If $(x+1)$ is a factor of $p(x)=3{x}^{2}+ax-2,$ then $a=$
q-7664.worked_solution:
According to the factor theorem, if $(x-r)$ is a factor of $p(x),$ then the root $x=r$ is also a root of $p(x).$ 

Here, we are considering the factor $(x+1).$ The root of this factor can be found by setting the factor equal to $0$ and solving:

$$
\begin{aligned}x+1 & =0 \\ x & =-1\end{aligned}
$$

According to the factor theorem, then, since $(x+1)$ is a factor of $p(x),$ the root $x=-1$ is also a root of $p(x).$ This means $p(-1)=0,$ so we have

$$
\begin{aligned}p(-1) & =0 \\ 3(-1)^{2}+a(-1)-2 & =0 \\ 3-a-2 & =0 \\ a & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

q-18946.name: Question 3
q-18946.problem: Given that $(x-2)$ and $(3x-1)$ are factors of $f(x)=3{x}^{3}+a{x}^{2}+bx+2,$ then $a+b=$
q-18946.worked_solution:
According to the factor theorem, if $(ax-b)$ is a factor of $f(x),$ then the root $x=\frac{b}{a}$ is also a root of $f(x).$ 

Here, we are considering the factors $(x-2)$ and $(3x-1).$ The roots of these factors can be found by setting the factors equal to $0$ and solving:

$$
\begin{aligned}x-2=0 & \,⇒\,x=2 \\ 3x-1=0 & \,⇒\,x=\frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

According to the factor theorem, then, since $(x-2)$ and $(3x-1)$ are factors of $f(x),$ the roots $x=2$ and $x=\frac{1}{3}$ are also roots of $f(x).$ This means $f(2)=0$ and $f(\frac{1}{3})=0,$ so we have

$$
\begin{aligned}f(2) & =0 \\ 3(2)^{3}+a(2)^{2}+b(2)+2 & =0 \\ 24+4a+2b+2 & =0 \\ 4a+2b & =-26 \\ 2a+b & =-13, \\  \\ f(\frac{1}{3}) & =0 \\ 3{(\frac{1}{3})}^{3}+a{(\frac{1}{3})}^{2}+b(\frac{1}{3})+2 & =0 \\ \frac{1}{9}+\frac{a}{9}+\frac{b}{3}+2 & =0 \\ 1+a+3b+18 & =0 \\ a+3b & =-19 \\ -2a-6b & =38.\end{aligned}
$$

This gives a system of equations

$$
\{\begin{aligned}2a+b=-13 \\ -2a-6b=38.\end{aligned}
$$

Adding the equations, we eliminate $a$ and get

$$
-5b=25\,⇒\,b=-5.
$$

Substituting $b=-5$ in either equation gives $a=-4.$ So our solutions are $a=-4$ and $b=-5.$ Finally then,

$$
a+b=-4+(-5)=-9.
$$

q-18942.name: Question 4
q-18942.problem: Given that $x$ and $(x+4)$ are factors of $f(x)=a{x}^{3}+11{x}^{2}-4x+b,$ determine $a+b.$
q-18942.worked_solution:
According to the factor theorem, if $(x-r)$ is a factor of $f(x),$ then the root $x=r$ is also a root of $f(x).$ 

Here, we are considering the factors $x$ and $(x+4).$ The roots of these factors can be found by setting the factors equal to $0$ and solving:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=0 & \,⇒\,x=0 \\ x+4=0 & \,⇒\,x=-4\end{aligned}
$$

According to the factor theorem, then, since $x$ and $(x+4)$ are factors of $f(x),$ the roots $x=0$ and $x=-4$ are also roots of $f(x).$ This means $f(0)=0$ and $f(-4)=0,$ so we have

$$
\begin{aligned}f(0) & =0 \\ a(0)^{3}+11(0)^{2}-4(0)+b & =0 \\ b & =0, \\  \\ f(-4) & =0 \\ a(-4)^{3}+11(-4)^{2}-4(-4)+b & =0 \\ -64a+176+16+b & =0 \\ -64a+192+0 & =0 \\ -64a & =-192 \\ a & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

So our solutions are $a=3$ and $b=0.$ Finally then,

$$
a+b=3+0=3.
$$
